terms.facility: A clinic with a biotech suite
terms.journalIntro: Write it together at the end of a job or mission. Advancements apply to the GM's copies; use each card's Save character file to send a player their update.
terms.restockDone: Restocked at a port: full load.
terms.emptyNote: Empty: it won't fire until you reload or recharge.
terms.tracksIntro: Shared by the whole crew. Borrowing, breaking the law, psionic slips and fame can mark a box; paying up, lying low and quiet work can clear one between jobs.

roles.name: Trader
roles.text: Trader: buys low and sells across a dozen systems; knows what everything is worth, and to whom.

roles.name: Broker
roles.text: Broker: finances ventures, buys and restructures debt, and writes the contracts everyone else signs.

roles.name: Corporate Agent
roles.text: Corporate agent: represents a company's interests far from head office, with its money and its orders.

roles.name: Smuggler
roles.text: Smuggler: moves what the Accord taxes, forbids or would rather not know about.

roles.name: Explorer
roles.text: Explorer: goes first into uncharted corridors and unclaimed worlds.

roles.name: Captain
roles.text: Captain: commands a ship and its crew, finds the work, makes the deals and makes the hard calls when the shooting starts.

roles.name: Pilot
roles.text: Pilot: flies anything, through anything, and gets paid for the impossible run.

roles.name: Gunner
roles.text: Gunner: runs the ship's weapons and point defense, and keeps them working when everything else is failing.

roles.name: Navigator
roles.text: Navigator: plots corridor transits, reads gravimetric drift and finds the way when the charts are wrong.

roles.name: Engineer
roles.text: Engineer: keeps the drive, the hull and everything else running, often with parts that don't fit.

roles.name: Medtech
roles.text: Medtech: the ship's medic and biotech operator, patching the crew between jobs and in the middle of them.

roles.name: Crew
roles.text: Crew: a general hand who stands watch, moves cargo, patches the hull and holds the airlock when someone tries to board.

roles.name: Prospector
roles.text: Prospector: finds the ore, the ruins or the claim that makes a fortune, then has to keep it.

roles.name: Salvager
roles.text: Salvager: strips wrecks and dead stations, and knows which ones should have stayed dead.

roles.name: AI Minder
roles.text: AI minder: bonded to a personal AI with a mind of its own, and trained to handle other AIs, from corporate systems to rogue minds.

roles.name: Scientist
roles.text: Scientist: studies what no one understands yet (alien biology, corridor physics, Hegemony ruins) for whoever funds it.

roles.name: Medic
roles.text: Medic: relief and field medicine, from refugee camps to the war's back lines.

roles.name: Liaison
roles.text: Liaison: speaks for the Accord, a world or a company between peoples who misunderstand each other.

roles.name: Missionary
roles.text: Missionary: carries a faith, a cause or a charity to people who didn't ask, and sometimes needed it.

roles.name: Journalist
roles.text: Journalist: asks the questions, follows the money, and broadcasts what the powerful wanted hidden.

roles.name: Cyberneticist
roles.text: Cyberneticist: designs, installs and repairs implants; part surgeon, part engineer, often working where the law can't see.

roles.name: Mercenary
roles.text: Mercenary: a professional soldier for the war's endless contracts, or anyone else who pays.

roles.name: Investigator
roles.text: Investigator: finds people, solves crimes and recovers stolen assets, for the law or for hire.

roles.name: Fixer
roles.text: Fixer: knows who can get anything done, and takes a cut of every introduction.

roles.name: Hacker
roles.text: Hacker: breaks into systems, ledgers and AIs; every network is a door.

roles.name: Augment
roles.text: Augment: rebuilt with implants (soldier, laborer or thrill-seeker); the body is the tool, and its upkeep and stigma are the problem.

skills: Negotiate, persuade, preach, calm a crowd
Markets, contracts, appraisal, finance and debt
Read people and other species, spot a lie, counsel
Search, examine evidence, follow the money
Fly ships and vehicles, chases, docking
Plot corridors, read gravimetric drift, find the way

origins.name: Human
origins.desc: Adaptable, socially restless, and remarkably willing to challenge established institutions. Three centuries of corridor travel have scattered humanity across dozens of colonies, governments and movements: generous and ruthless, often in the same crew.
traits: +2 to Commerce to fund, pitch or rescue a risky enterprise.
You bet bigger than you should. Accept the loss when the gamble turns.
+2 to Survival or Navigation when going where older peoples won't.
Old customs bore you. Accept the offense you cause.
+2 to Diplomacy to talk someone out of a ruinous debt, grudge or deal.
You can't refuse someone in need. Accept the cost of helping.

origins.name: Tessan
origins.desc: Large, scaled, exceptionally long-lived beings for whom contractual obligation is the foundation of civilization. Tessan dynasties lend, insure and arbitrate across hundreds of worlds; contact with humanity has split them between traditional creditors and reformers.
core: Long-lived: a Tessan remembers deals made before most humans' grandparents were born.
Bond: a contract a Tessan swears to is binding in law throughout Tessan space.
traits: +2 to Commerce to recall a debt, contract or precedent.
Your word binds you even when it hurts. Accept the cost of keeping it.
Once per scene, a hit that would mark 1 box marks none.
Your bulk and age make haste hard. Accept being left behind or late.
+2 to Diplomacy with those who owe your family.
Your dynasty's obligations become yours. Accept the duty when it calls.

origins.name: Kel
origins.desc: Chitin-plated social beings raised in immense hive-cities, analytical and cooperative. The Kel homeworld is burdened by inherited Tessan debt; their search for new markets triggered humanity's First Contact Crisis. Kel society is split between loyalists, reformers and radicals.
core: Hive-raised: after a day alone, −1 to all rolls until back among others.
Hard to read: others take −2 to Psychology to read a Kel's mood.
traits: +2 to Investigation or Science when working with at least one ally.
Being cut off from others unnerves you. Accept the panic or the poor choice.
+2 to Psychology to read another Kel, or to coordinate a group by scent and posture.
You expect every favor repaid. Accept the misunderstanding it causes.
+2 to Commerce to find who owes whom.
Your world's creditors, or its radicals, want your help. Accept the call.

origins.name: Mirrun
origins.desc: Smooth-skinned amphibians from a deep-ocean world, agile swimmers famous for their humor. Their skin detects minute pressure changes; Mirrun researchers lead the field in gravimetric resonance detection.
core: Amphibious: breathe water and swim at running speed; your skin must stay moist (−1 to all rolls after a day dry).
traits: +2 to Sensors to feel movement, engines or corridor resonance through a hull or floor.
You can't stand by while a sea is poisoned. Accept the fight with the extractors.
+2 to Athletics in water and zero-g.
Arid worlds wear you down. Accept the misery.
+2 to Diplomacy to defuse a tense meeting with a joke.
The joke comes out at the wrong moment. Accept the offense.

origins.name: Ylith
origins.desc: Hollow-boned, feathered gliders with broad wing-membranes and extraordinary vision. Their aerial city-states are renowned for navigation and cartography; confined spaces are profoundly uncomfortable for them.
core: Glide: in normal gravity, glide down any height safely.
Far sight: see detail at many times human range.
traits: +2 to Sensors and Firearms at long range.
Tight spaces unsettle you. Accept −2 or the detour.
+2 to Navigation to find a corridor instruments miss.
You look down on groundlings. Accept the resentment.
Falls and crushes hurt you more. Accept the injury.

origins.name: Ozhvek
origins.desc: Massive, radially symmetrical founders of the Hegemony, on six powerful limbs, with sensory clusters all around their upper bodies and lifespans near five centuries. Their ancient houses are divided over what the empire should become.
core: All-around senses: you can't be surprised from behind.
Massive: most ships, doors and furniture are too small; −2 to Stealth.
traits: +2 to Leadership with Hegemony subjects and soldiers.
Every former subject remembers the empire. Accept the hostility.
Once per fight, a hit that would mark 2 or more boxes marks one fewer.
You are always noticed. Accept the attention.
+2 to Sensors and Investigation to notice anything in a room.
Your house wants something of you. Accept the summons.

origins.name: Dresh
origins.desc: Dense, four-armed soldiers from a high-gravity world, armored in thick hide. Dresh legions were the Hegemony's ground forces for millennia; now their protectorates argue whether soldiers owe the throne, their commanders, or the people they protect.
core: Four arms: hold a weapon and still climb, carry or work.
Dermal armor: once per fight, a hit marks one fewer box.
Heavy-world: −1 to physical rolls in low gravity without boots or a frame.
traits: +2 to Firearms or Close Combat fighting beside an ally.
Old loyalties pull at you. Accept the conflict of duty.
+2 to Close Combat to grapple or hold.
Orders come easier than choices. Accept the mistake of obeying.
+2 to Body rolls to resist injury, fatigue or crushing force.
The Hegemony keeps lists. Accept the bounty hunter.

origins.name: Shivar
origins.desc: Tall, narrow beings of translucent tissue whose nervous systems share emotions in synchronized pulses. Their theology reads the corridors as cosmic order; their schism, between imperial zealots and moderates who see a universe of change, has fueled wars inside the Hegemony.
core: Empath: you share emotions instantly with nearby Shivar, and feel the strong emotions of anyone close by. (Empathy, not psionics.)
traits: +2 to Psychology to read anyone's feelings nearby.
Strong emotions around you overwhelm you. Accept the distraction.
+2 to Science or Navigation to read meaning in corridor patterns.
Zealots or moderates want you on their side. Accept the pressure.
+2 to Diplomacy to calm a frightened or angry crowd.
Your feelings show through your skin. Accept the lie that fails.

origins.name: Brulvek
origins.desc: Low, broad hexapods with powerful manipulator limbs and thick insulating hides, evolved among volcanoes and corrosive air. They built the Hegemony's shipyards; their engineers are sought everywhere for restoring machines centuries past replacement parts.
core: Furnace hide: heat, smoke and corrosive air mark one fewer box and don't impair you.
traits: +2 to Engineering to repair or restore ancient or unfamiliar machinery.
Your syndicate calls in a favor. Accept the job.
+2 to Survival in heat, fire and toxic environments.
Someone still pays your people to serve the empire. Accept the conflict.
+2 to Athletics to lift, haul or brace.
Home is failing. Accept the plea for money or help.

origins.name: Zhaq
origins.desc: Flexible, tripedal beings with segmented limbs and three independently focusing eyes. Isolated for six centuries by a corridor collapse, the Zhaq built free republics, and refused when the Hegemony came back. Their resistance inspires separatists everywhere.
core: Three eyes: watch several directions at once.
Torpor: slow your metabolism to outlast cold, hunger or entombment for weeks.
traits: +2 to Sensors to keep watch or spot an ambush.
You won't submit to an empire's demand. Accept the fight.
+2 to Survival to endure deprivation in torpor.
Your face means rebellion to the Hegemony. Accept the attention.
+2 to Athletics to squeeze, climb or balance.
Imperial customs you never learned trip you up. Accept the gaffe.

origins.name: Veyari
origins.desc: Small bipedal scholars with long, delicate fingers, soft scales and brains built for associative memory. Their neutral archives hold lost corridor data and ancient claims, which is why empires, corporations and zealots keep trying to seize them.
core: Associative memory: recall anything you have experienced in detail.
traits: +2 to Science or Investigation to recall history, precedent or old data.
You won't let records be destroyed. Accept the risk to save them.
+2 to Diplomacy to be accepted as neutral by both sides.
Someone wants what you remember. Accept the pursuit.
+2 to Investigation to spot what changed in a place you've seen before.
You're easy to overpower. Accept the danger.

origins.name: Eshuum
origins.desc: Colonial organisms: an Eshuum person is a community of semi-independent biological units joined into one mind. They govern by consensus, and oppose forced separation and experiments on intelligent beings.
core: Detachable units: send a small unit to scout a short distance; it reports what it senses.
Many bodies: once per fight, a hit that would mark 2 or more boxes marks one fewer as units are lost.
traits: +2 to Sensors or Stealth using a detached unit.
Forced separation is horror to you. Accept the risk to prevent it.
+2 to Psychology to find what a group truly agrees on.
Hegemony researchers want specimens. Accept the danger.
+2 to Engineering or Medicine by reshaping units into fine tools.
You must reach inner consensus. Accept the delay.

origins.name: Khaum
origins.desc: Massive, eyeless burrowers with sensory whiskers and powerful digging limbs, whose cavern nations run for hundreds of kilometers underground. Cautious and long-planning, they have sheltered refugees from many Hegemony campaigns.
core: Eyeless: perceive by pressure and vibration; darkness means nothing, but you can't read screens or print without aids.
Burrower: dig through earth and soft rock.
Massive: −2 to Stealth; most doors are too small.
traits: +2 to Sensors to feel movement, footsteps or tunnels through the ground.
Open skies and unfamiliar places unsettle you. Accept the hesitation.
+2 to Athletics to dig, break or brace rock.
You shelter the hunted. Accept the danger they bring.
+2 to Engineering when you have time to plan.
You refuse protection that demands obedience. Accept the cost.

origins.name: Vael
origins.desc: Long, light-boned beings with four manipulator limbs, born in low gravity. Their homeworld died in an ancient stellar catastrophe; their living fleets now roam the corridors trading, repairing and carrying peoples between systems.
core: Zero-g native: no penalty in zero gravity.
Low-gravity body: −1 to physical rolls in standard gravity without an exo-frame.
traits: +2 to Athletics and Firearms in zero-g.
The flotilla's needs come before yours. Accept the call.
+2 to Commerce in flotilla markets and ports.
Gravity wells exhaust you. Accept the strain.
+2 to Engineering to keep a habitat or ship running on nothing.
Every side doubts the fleets. Accept the search or the suspicion.

origins.name: Thrum
origins.desc: Broad, soft-bodied beings whose internal cavities make low-frequency resonance; they speak in overlapping harmonies humans can't reproduce. Their acoustic science found the patterns in corridor fluctuations; they refuse to let it become weapons.
core: Resonance: speak and hear through walls and floors; you need a translator for most other languages.
traits: +2 to Sensors to map a space or find a void by sound.
You won't let your work become a weapon. Accept the cost of refusing.
+2 to Leadership or Diplomacy addressing a group.
Translators mangle you. Accept the misunderstanding.
+2 to Navigation or Science reading corridor fluctuations.
You bruise easily. Accept the injury.

origins.name: Corvani
origins.desc: Radially arranged, five-limbed beings with photosensitive skin, from forests where cooperation meant survival. They treat technology as ecology, and their restoration teams heal worlds the Hegemony stripped, often against mining corporations.
core: Photosynthetic: after days without light you weaken (−1 to all rolls) until you rest under light.
traits: +2 to Science to heal or understand a damaged ecosystem.
You won't let a world be poisoned. Accept the fight.
+2 to Engineering with biological or grown technology.
Dark ships and stations drain you. Accept the weakness.
+2 to Medicine with biotech and alien biology.
Mining companies know your face. Accept their lawyers or worse.

origins.name: Uxarra
origins.desc: Flexible, partly hydrostatic beings whose skin changes color, texture and sheen. Their homeworld's wild climates made them adaptable and self-reliant, and their camouflage has earned them an unfair reputation for deceit.
core: Chromatic skin: change color and texture at will.
traits: +2 to Stealth when still or moving slowly.
Others assume you're hiding something. Accept the suspicion.
+2 to Survival in extreme or changing environments.
You can't settle. Accept the urge to move on.
+2 to Athletics or Medicine to reach and save someone in a disaster.
You go back for the last one. Accept the risk.

origins.name: Sen
origins.desc: Compact, slow-moving beings in layered mineral shells who live more than a thousand years. Their experiments have run for centuries; they have watched empires rise and fall, and their warnings about corridor instability carry great weight.
core: Shell: once per fight, a hit marks one fewer box.
Slow: you always act last in a fight, and Move −1.
traits: +2 to Science or Investigation when you take your time.
You think in decades. Accept being too late.
+2 to Navigation to predict corridor behavior.
You'd rather observe than act. Accept the cost of waiting.
+2 to Will to stay calm under fear, pressure or torture.
You can't run. Accept being caught.

origins.name: Joruun
origins.desc: Tall, powerful bipeds with thick skin, sensory ridges and acute hearing, from a cold, storm-wracked world. Their confederation has fought the Hegemony for centuries, built to keep resisting after its leaders fall.
core: Cold-hardy: cold and storms don't impair you.
traits: Your league needs you. Accept the call to arms.
+2 to Leadership to rally others after a leader falls.
You hate the Hegemony. Accept the reckless choice.
+2 to Firearms when holding a fortified position.
You say what you think. Accept the offense.

origins.name: Qor
origins.desc: Silicon-based beings of slowly growing crystal with distributed nervous systems, speaking by electromagnetic and mechanical oscillation. Masters of materials and computation, the Qor take Tessan capital but refuse debts that threaten sovereignty.
core: Crystalline: immune to vacuum, toxins and disease; you need a translator to speak with most species.
Slow time sense: −1 to Psychology with fast-living peoples.
Heavy crystal: Move −1.
traits: +2 to Engineering with materials, armor and hull structures.
You won't accept terms that bind your world. Accept the lost deal.
You misjudge how quickly others act. Accept the delay.
+2 to Survival in vacuum and extreme environments.
Prospectors eye your homeworld. Accept the confrontation.

origins.name: Ommek
origins.desc: Small, heavily articulated beings with many fine manipulators and exquisite touch, makers of robots, AI and automated ships. Their technocratic republics demand review of every major technology, and their defenses have made conquest too expensive.
core: Fine manipulators: Engineering is Trained for free.
traits: You insist on checking first. Accept the delay.
+2 to Computers with robots, drones and AI.
The Hegemony wants your knowledge. Accept the spy or the kidnapper.
+2 to Engineering or Computers to secure a position or system.
You're easily overpowered. Accept the danger.

origins.name: Vesh
origins.desc: Slender quadrupeds who handle tools with prehensile sensory tendrils, and who reached the corridors only 24 years ago. Their governments struggle to stay independent while learning from civilizations thousands of years older, and humans recognize the struggle.
core: Quick on four legs: Move +1.
traits: +2 to Investigation to notice what old hands take for granted.
You don't know the rules everyone else knows. Accept the gaffe.
+2 to Sensors to feel air currents and nearby movement.
Your government wants a favor. Accept the request.
+2 to Athletics to run or leap.
Everyone has a deal for you. Accept the bad bargain.

origins.name: Uth
origins.desc: Compact, thick-skinned beings with broad manipulators and complex chemical senses, whose civilization the Hegemony destroyed millennia ago. Uth communities live everywhere, keeping family history and memory; many work to reclaim their worlds, many refuse to be defined by loss.
core: Chemical senses: identify people and substances by scent.
traits: +2 to Investigation to track or identify by scent.
The reclamation movement asks your help. Accept the call.
+2 to Streetwise to find an Uth community and its help in any port.
The Hegemony's name sets you off. Accept the reckless choice.
+2 to Diplomacy using shared history or old obligations.
Others see only your people's history. Accept the frustration.

origins.name: Draelin
origins.desc: Long, serpentine beings with two long arms and no legs, who sense electromagnetic fields, from a world of wild magnetic fields. Their cartographic guilds keep the best corridor charts in known space, and have sold them to both sides of more than one war.
core: Field sense: feel electromagnetic fields, live wiring and active machinery nearby.
Navigation is Trained for free.
traits: Your guild sells your secrets to the other side. Accept the betrayal.
+2 to Sensors to find hidden machinery or follow a power line.
You must decide who gets safe passage. Accept the guild's anger.
+2 to Athletics to squeeze, coil and climb where legs can't.
Strong fields disorient you. Accept the stumble.

origins.name: Zethri
origins.desc: Small, agile beings with four limbs, a prehensile tail and broad reflective eyes adapted to dim light. A corridor collapse isolated their colonies for centuries; reconnected, they found strangers who share their name, and now work at reunification.
core: Dim-adapted: see in near-darkness; −1 to Agility-based rolls in bright light.
traits: +2 to Sensors and Stealth in darkness.
Bright light blinds you at the worst moment. Accept the stumble.
+2 to Athletics to climb, hang or hold on in zero-g.
Other Zethri colonies see you as a foreigner. Accept the mistrust.
+2 to Engineering or Survival to make a place self-sufficient.
Your cluster's factions disagree about you. Accept the dispute.

allegiances: concord
The Concord
Once per job, consular help, credentials or a Concord navy contact.
Duty: Concord interests come first, even when they're wrong.
dynasty
A Tessan Dynasty
Once per job, credit, insurance or priority corridor access.
Duty: protect the dynasty's contracts, and collect what's owed.
corp
A Corporation
Once per job, transport, gear or an expense account.
Duty: the company's profits, and its secrets.
house
A Hegemony House
Once per job, imperial passes, an audience or house soldiers.
Duty: the house's ambitions in the succession wars.
zhaq
The Zhaq Free Republics
Once per job, a safehouse, weapons or a resistance cell.
Duty: the cause; smuggle, sabotage, shelter fugitives.
archives
The Veyari Archives
Once per job, records, lost corridor data or an archivist's research.
Duty: recover and preserve knowledge, whoever wants it buried.
guild
A Draelin Cartographic Guild
Once per job, current corridor charts or a navigator.
Duty: guild fees and guild secrets; never sell charts outside the guild.
flotilla
A Vael Flotilla
Once per job, passage, repairs or a berth anywhere the fleet goes.
Duty: the flotilla's neutrality, and its needs.
relief
A Relief Mission
Once per job, medical supplies, shelter or refugee contacts.
Duty: aid comes first, even in the middle of a job.
syndicate
A Syndicate
Once per job, fences, smuggling routes or forged papers.
Duty: the syndicate's cut, and its jobs.
quiet
The Quiet Network
Once per job, false test results, a safe route or a new identity for a psionic.
Duty: shelter other psionics, at any risk.
reasons: Fortune
There's money out here for anyone with nerve, and I intend to make mine.
Knowledge
The galaxy is full of things no one understands yet. I want to be first.
New worlds
Somewhere past the next corridor there's a place to build something new.
Helping
People out here need help, and I can give it.
Freedom
No empire, no creditor, no one owns me.
Debt
I owe more than I can ever repay, unless I take every job.
Vengeance
Someone took everything from me. I'll find them.
Faith
I carry a truth worth sharing, even with those who don't want it.
Exile
I can't go home. The crew is home now.
The thrill
Nothing feels like a corridor jump into the unknown.
connections: Shipmates
We've flown together for years and trust each other with our lives.
They saved my life
They pulled me out of a wreck, a riot or a Mandate screening.
I saved theirs
I got them off a dying station, and they haven't forgotten.
Business partners
We split everything, the profits and the debts.
Rivals
We want the same contract, the same charts or the same discovery.
Same homeworld
We grew up in the same place and know each other's families.
An unpaid debt
I owe them money or a favor, and I haven't paid yet.
A shared secret
We know what really happened on that job. No one else does.
Mentor
They taught me everything I know about the job.
Strange friends
Our peoples were enemies; we found out we aren't.
advantages: +2 to Commerce when negotiating a price, a loan or a contract.
No translator needed for common languages; +2 to Diplomacy in first meetings with a new species.
+2 to Psychology or Science to understand an unfamiliar species.
+2 to Streetwise to find goods, work or a person.
+2 to Navigation to find a safe route through an unstable corridor.
+2 to Piloting in a chase or a dangerous maneuver.
+2 to Firearms after spending an action aiming at the same target.
+2 to Medicine to stabilize a patient in the field.
+2 to Computers to break security or cover your tracks.
+2 to Science on a study you can repeat or take time over.
+2 to Engineering or Commerce to judge what wreckage is worth.
You own a small ship (crewed by the party), with a loan: start with one box of Debt.
A personal AI that can assist Computers, Sensors and Investigation rolls (AI Minders have one already).
A personal drone; +2 to Sensors when scouting or Engineering when repairing with it.
Biotech modifications: +2 to Body rolls against disease, toxins and radiation.
+2 to Athletics or Close Combat where strength matters. It shows, and needs upkeep.
+2 to Sensors or Investigation by sight; see in low light. It shows, and needs upkeep.
+2 to Computers when jacked in directly. A hostile system can strike back.
+1 Dodge, and +2 to act first in a fight. It shows on scans.
+2 to Will to keep acting under fire, fear or pressure.
You have psionic potential: you can learn psionic powers (see Psionics and the Mandates). Take the Unregistered complication unless the GM agrees otherwise.
You start play with three data records, each a secret your work or your people taught you: something in no database or published record. They grant no bonus: they let you act on what you know.
complications: You owe a dynasty, a bank or a syndicate. Accept the collector's demand.
You're a psionic who has never been tested, or has a forged result. Accept the danger at every screening and checkpoint.
A government, house or corporation wants you. Accept the hunters.
An imperial house has put a price on you. Accept the bounty hunter.
Your implants need parts, power and care. Accept the cost or the malfunction.
You won't compromise your principles. Accept the cost of keeping them.
You can't walk away from profit. Accept the risk to grab it.
Someone is always a step ahead or behind you. Accept their interference.
Your employer owns your contract. Accept the order you don't like.
You keep your word, your oaths and your people's customs. Accept the setback.
You lived when others didn't. Accept the reckless choice to make it right.
A strange signal or ruin pulls you in. Accept the detour or the danger.
You shield the weak at your own risk. Accept the cost.
You lean on combat stims or calm-patches. Accept the craving or the crash.
You can't go home. Accept the scorn or the hunters of your own people.
You know a corridor, a crime or a name someone would kill to bury. Accept the danger.
You jump first and think later. Accept the danger.
You won't trust a machine mind. Accept the cost of refusing its help.
You misread other peoples' customs. Accept the misunderstanding.

debtbound: A collector waits at the dock
A creditor offers to forgive it for a favor
unregistered: A Mandate screening at the corridor gate
Someone saw your power and knows what it means
wanted: Your face on a station's watch list
A familiar uniform in the crowd
An old associate sells you out
bounty: A hunter in the next berth
upkeep: A part fails at the worst moment
idealist: The easy way means hurting innocents
Your employer asks you to look away
greedy: A fortune on the table, and a trap around it
A partner's share could be yours
The cargo is worth more than the job
leash: The company wants the cargo, not the people
guilt: Someone in the same danger as before
mystery: A signal on a dead channel
protects: A friend about to be left behind
Someone volunteers for a deadly task in your place
exile: Your people on the same station
secret: A powerful figure asks what you know
reckless: A closed door in a dangerous place
The careful plan takes too long
distrustai: The AI offers the only way through
culture: A joke that isn't funny to them

equipment: Twelve rounds. Hits mark 2 boxes. Short range.
Twenty shots per cell; silent, no recoil. Hits mark 2 boxes. Short range.
Thirty rounds; can fire bursts. Hits mark 2 boxes. Medium range.
Ten shots per cell. Hits mark 3 boxes and leave the target Dying. Medium range.
The target rolls Body −2: failure, out for the scene; success, −2 on their next action. Marks no box. Close range.
A humming blade. Hits mark 2 boxes.
Once per fight, a hit that marks 2 or more boxes marks one fewer. Shows under scans.
A hardened security shield: +1 to Block against blades, fists and thrown objects. It won't stop a slug or a beam. −2 to Stealth while you carry it.
Air for six hours in vacuum or poison atmosphere.
Biotech dressings, stims and a scanner. Needed to stabilize a patient and give field treatment.
Needed for most Engineering in the field.
A hacking rig. Needed for most Computers work against secured systems.
Handheld sensor. Needed for most Sensors work away from a ship.
A small flying drone that can scout and relay what it sees.
Translates most known languages, slowly. Thrum and Qor need one to talk with most peoples.
A light powered frame: no gravity penalty for Vael and others built for low gravity.

An armored vac suit: air for six hours in vacuum or poison atmosphere, and once per fight a hit that marks 2 or more boxes marks one fewer. −1 to Athletics and Stealth while you wear it; a breach is the GM's call. Not with other armor.

A powered military frame: +2 to Athletics to lift, carry, climb or break things, your unarmed blows mark 2 boxes, and you carry a heavy weapon one-handed. Its plating works as body armor: once per fight, a 2+ box hit marks one fewer. −2 to Stealth; needs a fresh power cell each day. Not with other armor.

Legion-grade, sealed and powered: hits that would mark 1 box mark nothing, and once per fight a hit that marks 2 or more boxes marks one fewer. Air for six hours, and the strength of a combat exoskeleton. −2 to Stealth, any scanner picks it up, and it needs a fresh power cell each day. A shot at the power pack (−2 to hit) can lock it up until someone spends an action freeing you. Needs the Powered Armor Edge. Not with other armor.

A security or industrial suit, sold where the law allows it: once per fight a hit that would mark 1 box marks nothing, and once per fight a 2+ box hit marks one fewer. Air for six hours, and the strength of a combat exoskeleton. −2 to Stealth and a power cell each day. Registered: any scanner reads its owner. Needs the Powered Armor Edge. Not with other armor.

Built by an illicit armorer in some remote colony: protects like a commercial suit, but it's Temperamental: on a natural 17 or 18 on any physical roll, the suit seizes until someone spends an action freeing you. It drinks a power cell twice a day, and it's contraband everywhere but where it was made. Needs the Powered Armor Edge. Not with other armor.
Accord transit permits and a clean (or convincing) Mandate record.

Up to 3× light speed (civilian 1–2×). In-system: hours. Between stars: light-years ÷ 3 in years. Not in corridors, near mouths or deep in gravity wells.

One order an exchange: Command (Leadership, +2 to a station), Read the enemy (Psychology), Hail (Diplomacy or Deception vs Will), Rally (Leadership).
Debt (what you owe), Heat (who's after you), Reputation (who knows you), Hull (your ship). 4 boxes each; clear by paying up, lying low, quiet work or a dock between jobs.

pregens.role: A young reformer cut off by her dynasty's old creditors for writing off a client world's debt. She trades on her own now, and keeps her word.
pregens.reason: No empire, no creditor, no one owns me.

pregens.name: Kesh of the Seventh Hive
pregens.role: Scouts new markets to pay down her homeworld's debt, and wonders more each year whether the radicals are right.
pregens.reason: I owe more than I can ever repay, unless I take every job.
pregens.connection: Ilvi Saradh's AI found the corridor Kesh's hive needed; Kesh owes them both.

comp.trigger: A creditor offers to forgive it for a favor

gear.use: surveying a world: minerals, water and life signs

pregens.name: Rook
pregens.role: Rebuilt after the Zhaq border war with a cyber-arm and reflex wiring. The implant payments are overdue, and the company that made them knows where Rook drinks.
pregens.reason: I can't go home. The crew is home now.
pregens.connection: Brakka was on the other side of that border war. They found out over a drink, and stayed friends.

pregens.name: Ilvi Saradh
pregens.role: A guild navigator whose AI partner, Quill, remembers a corridor the guild says doesn't exist.
pregens.reason: The galaxy is full of things no one understands yet. I want to be first.
pregens.connection: Quill found the corridor Kesh's hive needed. Ilvi never told the guild.

gear.use: breaking old guild encryption and recovering lost navigation data

pregens.name: Dr. Anwe Tal
pregens.role: Rebuilding a world the Hegemony strip-mined, against a mining corporation's lawyers and, lately, its guns.
pregens.reason: People out here need help, and I can give it.
pregens.connection: Sable cleaned up the corporation's files that proved Anwe's case, and asked nothing for it.
pregens.contact: A Veyari archivist who keeps the old survey records of her world

pregens.name: Brakka
pregens.role: A legionary who deserted rather than burn a Zhaq city. The Hegemony wants him back, or dead.
pregens.reason: Someone took everything from me. I'll find them.
pregens.connection: Rook fought him across the Zhaq border once. Now Rook watches his back.

comp.trigger: A hunter in the next berth

pregens.reason: No empire, no creditor, no one owns me.
pregens.connection: Sable cleaned up the files that proved Dr. Anwe Tal's case, for nothing. Anwe wonders why.

gmGuide.title: Fracture Lines GM's Guide
gmGuide.subtitle: Running the space opera: jobs, threats, enemy ships and the GM's tools
gmGuide.intro: This book is for whoever runs the game, and anyone can read it. It gathers what the GM reaches for at the table: job seeds, the threats and enemy ships with their numbers, and how to use the GM view's battle map and Encounter panel. The rules themselves are in the **Players' Guide**; this book builds on them.
gmGuide.playersNote: The material for running the game (job seeds, the threats and enemy ships, and the GM's tools) is in a companion book, the **GM's Guide**.

discovery.subject: an alien species, a derelict technology, an uncharted world behind a collapsed corridor, or a faction's intentions
discovery.uncover: how it is beaten, or how it is used
kinds: How it is beaten: a predator's or a hostile system's weakness
How it is used: a species' customs that allow negotiation, a derelict's systems that allow operating it
phases: Effects without a cause: a signal no one can read, a derelict that powers up, a crew that won't answer. You may suspect, but nothing is confirmed.

Name it: the species, the technology, the world, the faction's aim. This is the gate: until its identity is confirmed, what you know about a kind of subject doesn't yet apply to this one, and your theories stay suspicions. You can still form hypotheses, test them and take ordinary precautions, and whatever is actually true of it works.
Learn how it is beaten, or how it is used. Filling this phase fills the clock and earns a data record for what you established.

threat.name: Countdown
threat.text: The threat is often the situation itself: failing life support, a collapsing corridor, a reactor going critical, a first-contact window closing. A Countdown is a hard timer: it ticks with time (each scene, or each hour the GM sets), whatever the crew does. Several clocks can race the same Countdown: one to understand the alien and one to repair the ship, all needed before it ends.

costs: overt scanning of restricted space, slicing into a faction's systems, provoking their security
asking every port about the derelict, broadcasting on open channels, a first contact that gets noticed
close passes to the anomaly, pushing the sensors past their limits, docking with the unknown
methods: Passive first, active if you must (active scanning of restricted space ticks Heat).
Samples, spectra, biology, the physics of the drive.
Logs, firmware, the derelict's own records, a faction's network.
Their customs, their fears, what their silence means.
Brokers, archives, a captain who's been there.
Walk the world, chart the collapsed corridor, map the derelict deck by deck.

discovery.origins: A character's species can suit a method: senses, memory, psionics or a people's own history with the subject. A species that touches minds can advance a phase with Psionics, at the GM's call.

your own scans and samples, or a careful field test

a trusted archive, another ship's logs, a species' own historians. A source's reputation alone doesn't make it right, but a reliable record can establish a fact without anyone repeating a dangerous test
what an alien, an AI or a faction tells you, supported by evidence
discovery.anyway: A real weakness works whoever uses it, data record or no data record: a predator's blind spot or a system's back door works for anyone who finds it. Operating unfamiliar technology, or dealing by a species' customs, still needs the right procedure, the knowledge and the skill.
